content:
This July, Apple updated its TestFlight app with basic search functionality. You might think such a simple update would be universally welcomed, but the same TestFlight update introduced a rather frustrating bug for many users.

Personally, I wasn't noticeably affected by this bug. Because of that, I initially considered the TestFlight update a simple but significant improvement.

Sometimes, a small change can have a big impact. This is especially true for users with a large number of beta apps when it comes to Apple's latest TestFlight update. Apple has just updated TestFlight for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and other platforms. The new version 4.3 added "a search field to quickly find apps."

In hindsight, I did notice something odd, which I noted at the end of the article (though I had it exactly backwards):

I think the reason I didn't realize this was a bug is because two years ago I kept several years' worth of TestFlight beta apps to "merge" my previously separate iCloud and App Store Apple accounts. It wasn't the most convenient approach, but it was worth it for me.

Regardless, the TestFlight bug did not escape the notice of MacStories' John Vorhees:

So, when I saw Zac Hall's article on 9to5Mac about TestFlight gaining a search field, you can imagine my excitement. I thought: "Finally!" I immediately stopped what I was doing to update the app. […] Unfortunately, there's a big "but" in this story. In the old days, TestFlight betas were listed in reverse chronological order, which I personally loved. […] Today, these expired betas are scattered alphabetically among the currently active TestFlight betas, and the list of expired betas seems to have expanded to include every beta I've ever participated in. I roughly counted nearly 800 app entries for me. As you can imagine, very few of them are active betas. The search function helps, but scrolling is no longer a viable way to find things.

Then in August, John Gruber wrote about the TestFlight update and bug on Daring Fireball:

Last night, more than a month after this bug appeared (and was pointed out by Vorhees), Apple finally updated TestFlight for the first time. Although the release notes only mention bug fixes, this update does indeed fix the bug in question.

TestFlight version 4.3.1 is the fix for users affected by this regression.
